mode: standalone fallback (proposed destinations not being added); ids are the if_declined_standalone ids, plus town-centre spots (ids suffixed -town so they cannot collide with proposed destination ids)
shared_notes: Fetched with scripts/curation/fetch.ts; nothing was BLOCKED (no captcha/403): NPWS, crystalcastle.com.au, tropicalfruitworld.com.au (+ its Rezdy page), gallery.tweed.nsw.gov.au, lismoregallery.org, byronbaydivecentre.com.au all loaded 200. No in-app browser check needed.

resolve-pin.py reached Overpass only through a mirror (overpass-api.de returned nothing from this machine), so the first run fell back to Photon (OSM-derived) and graded most single features LOW; a second run via the maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror (a scratch copy of the script, repo untouched) upgraded Main Beach, Seven Mile Beach, Lake Ainsworth, Crystal Castle, Tweed Regional Gallery, Iluka Nature Reserve and the Wollumbin/Nightcap/Toonumbar visitor points. The mirror then throttled, so Tallow, Cabarita, Lighthouse Beach, The Pass, towns and Tropical Fruit World stay LOW-by-tool (single OSM feature via Photon) and are flagged per entry for the orchestrator to accept or hold.
Town pins are OSM place nodes / town-centre points, accurate to roughly 0.3-1 km; resolve-pin has no precise feature type for a town.

NPWS park-entry fees for this region: Cape Byron lighthouse/lawn and information centre $10 per vehicle per hour (max 1 h per vehicle per day, annual passes included, $4 motorcycles); Captain Cook lookout, Cosy Corner, The Pass and Bawaii $5 per vehicle per hour; Bundjalung National Park $8 per vehicle per day. No fee is listed for Wollumbin, Nightcap, Toonumbar or Iluka Nature Reserve. Passes: All Parks $190/yr, Multi Parks $65/yr, Country Parks $45/yr, Single Country Park $22/yr.

CURRENT CLOSURES (NPWS local-alerts pages, read 2026-10-18/19): Wollumbin summit track and summit closed until further notice (alert since 30 Jun 2023, reviewed 3 Oct 2026); Nightcap Range Road closed (2022 flood landslip) to 31 Dec 2026, Minyon Falls lookout reachable via Minyon Falls Road only; Toonumbar Forest Drive/Cox's Road closed to about 31 Oct 2026 and Sherwood/Murray Scrub lookouts closed; Cape Byron Lighthouse Cafe closed from 31 May 2026.

Point Danger: Wikipedia lists the lighthouse in Queensland (headland between Coolangatta and Tweed Heads). The standalone timezone Australia/Sydney in placement may need to be Australia/Brisbane for this one spot; decision for the orchestrator.
No Wikivoyage page exists for Brunswick Heads (404); Wikivoyage Ballina is only a disambiguation page and Lismore the disambiguation page (the town is at Lismore_(New_South_Wales)).

entries.name: Cape Byron Lighthouse
entries.hours: Lawn 8:00 AM – sunset; museum 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM
entries.cost_note: AUD 10 is the NPWS pay-parking fee at the lighthouse carpark ($10 per vehicle per hour, max 1 hour per vehicle per calendar day, annual passes included); there is no separate entry charge on foot (walking up from town is free). Lighthouse and Maritime Museum guided tours run on limited days/times, price not published on the page.

facts.claim: Cape Byron Lighthouse sits on Australia's most easterly point; guided tours of the lighthouse or the Maritime Museum are available on limited days and times (email npws.tweedbyron@environment.nsw.gov.au or phone 02 6639 8300).

Park entry fees: Cape Byron Lighthouse lawn and Information Centre $10 per vehicle per hour ($4 motorcycles), maximum 1 hour per vehicle per calendar day including all NPWS annual passholders; Captain Cook lookout, Cosy Corner and The Pass $5 per vehicle per hour.

Lighthouse lawn is open 8am to sunset; the Maritime Museum in the former Lighthouse Keeper's office is open 10am to 4pm daily; the conservation area is open all hours but may close for weather or fire danger.
Walgun Cape Byron Information Centre is open 9.30am to 4.30pm daily, closed Christmas Day.
Cape Byron Lighthouse Cafe closed from 31 May 2026 (NPWS alert applies to 26 Feb 2027; future options being assessed).
Regular sightings of turtles, dolphins and humpback whales from the point; the lighthouse was operated by resident keepers until 1989 and is now automated.
The walk from town to the lighthouse is about 20 min from the start of the walk along the beach; the full walking track is a 3.7 km loop around the cape.

unverified: Guided-tour prices and the days/times of lighthouse and museum tours (NPWS says "limited days and times"; no price on the page).
Parking fee is as shown on NPWS pages fetched 2026-10-18 and can change.

entries.hours: Daily snorkel and dive trips by boat; book ahead

facts.claim: Nguthungulli Julian Rocks Nature Reserve was created in March 1961 and covers 0.4 ha.

Julian Rocks lie just 2.5 km out from Cape Byron, within Cape Byron Marine Park where temperate and tropical waters meet; the reserve is a sanctuary zone; over 1000 marine species including sea turtles, humpback whales, dolphins, rays and sharks; six main sites from 6 to 24 m.
Most diving at Byron is at Julian Rocks, only five minutes off shore, depths 5-25 m, suitable for snorkelling.
Byron Bay Dive Centre snorkel tour from A$119 (3 hours, min. 10 yrs); Turtle School + Snorkelling from A$149 (4 hours); Fun Dive from A$180 (2.5 hours, min. 12 yrs).

unverified: Prices are "from" prices on the operator's homepage, 2026-10-18; other operators (Sundive etc.) not priced.

A small coastal holiday village at the mouth of the Brunswick River; Torakina Beach is within the breakwater and a white sandy surf beach stretches to the south; the north bank is a protected rainforest and the south bank a harbour and small marina; it has retained its traditional seaside village atmosphere with timber bridges.
Brunswick Heads has a Visitor Information Centre, police station and post office (OSM features).

facts.claim: Lennox Head is a small coastal town between Byron Bay and Ballina known for surfing, windsurfing and kite sailing, with a relaxed village atmosphere.
Pat Morton lookout (at Lennox Point) offers views of the village and Seven Mile Beach towards Broken Head; the coast from Flat Rock to Lennox Point is the Lennox National Surfing Reserve.
Lennox Point is popular with surfers for a famous long right-hand break; hang-gliders launch from its 65 m cliff; good for watching dolphins and whale migrations.
Lake Ainsworth, a tannin-stained freshwater lake, lies at the northern edge of the village.

The reef off the southern end, the Moat/Boat Channel, is within Cape Byron Marine Park and good for snorkelling.

entries.name: Wollumbin National Park
entries.hours: Gate on Mount Warning Road 7:00 AM – 5:00 PM in winter, 7:00 AM – 6:00 PM in summer (daylight saving)
entries.cost_note: No park entry fee is listed on the NPWS pages read (the Bundjalung page, by contrast, lists $8 per vehicle). Summit track CLOSED.
entries.ticketUrl_note: Loaded 200, title "Wollumbin National Park | NSW National Parks"; managing agency.
entries.coordinates_source: osm trail midpoint "Lyrebird Track" (Overpass way) + osm tourism=viewpoint "Lyrebird Lookout" -28.398038,153.283707 (40 m): resolve-pin.py HIGH. Visitor point is the Breakfast Creek end of Mount Warning Road (carpark 3.5 km from Mount Warning Road turn-off, NPWS); the summit track is closed, so the pin is the open Lyrebird walk, not the peak (Mount Warning peak is -28.397824,153.271568)

facts.claim: Wollumbin (Mount Warning) summit track and Aboriginal Place remain closed; NPWS closed-area alert: summit track and the summit are closed until further notice (alert applies from 30 Jun 2023, last reviewed 3 Oct 2026). Korrumbyn Creek picnic area, Lyrebird walking track and visitor facilities at Breakfast Creek remain open; parking is limited.
Visitors are asked to respect Bundjalung wishes and not climb the summit track (8.8 km return, grade 5, 5-6 hrs when open).
Lyrebird track: 0.3 km return, 15-30 min, grade 3, open 7am-5pm winter and 7am-6pm summer (daylight saving), from Mount Warning Road across Breakfast Creek to a lookout in rainforest.

The park is open but may close at times due to perceived risk; the gate on Mount Warning Road may close from 5pm in winter and 6pm in summer and reopen at 7am. Carpark is about 3.5 km along Mount Warning Road, ~12 km from Murwillumbah toward Uki.
Wollumbin rises to 1,157 m, a remnant central vent of an ancient volcano; highly significant to Aboriginal people, particularly the Bundjalung nation.
Pets are not permitted; limited mobile reception.

unverified: Whether the summit will reopen (NPWS: decisions will follow the wishes of Aboriginal custodians).
NPWS does not state a park entry fee; free is inferred from the absence of a fee section.
entries.bio_note: Placement bio ("summit track is closed, a short lookout walk remains") is confirmed current as of 2026-10-18. Mount Warning is an alias.

facts.claim: Point Danger Light, also known as the Captain Cook Memorial Light, is an active lighthouse on Point Danger, a headland between Coolangatta and Tweed Heads marking the Queensland-NSW border; built 1971 to commemorate the bicentennial of Cook's 1770 voyage; it lays claim to being the first lighthouse in the world to experiment with a laser light source.
Wikipedia lists the lighthouse location as Point Danger, Queensland.
James Cook named Point Danger in 1770, but the name later became attached to the headland north of the Tweed River mouth; the headland to the south, now Fingal Head, was Cook's Point Danger.
The NSW-Queensland border runs parallel to the beach for some kilometres before ending at the headland north of the Tweed River mouth.

unverified: "Whale watching" in the placement bio not confirmed in sources read for this headland.
Which side of the border the pin lies on: Wikipedia places the lighthouse in Queensland.
entries.bio_note: Placement bio "NSW-Queensland border meets the sea" supported; do not say it is in NSW.

coordinates_check.note: Placement point -28.2,153.57084 was the OSM feature itself (Photon); resolve-pin re-run confirms, the near-round latitude is real.

facts.claim: Fingal Head is a village about 5 km south of the NSW-Queensland border; the headland and offshore Cook Island were first sighted by Cook in 1770.

Interlocking basalt columns on the north-east side of the headland were called the "Giants Causeway"; the headland, Cook Island and Danger Reefs were formed by a lava flow from the extinct Tweed Volcano; there are walking tracks all over the area.
The stone lighthouse built in 1878 is only seven metres high; the headland adds height (focal plane 24 m above sea level).
Wikivoyage: many kilometres of isolated beaches; the headland is a volcanic rock headland originally named Point Danger by Cook.

unverified: Whether the lighthouse interior is open to visitors (not stated); Wikipedia calls it the Fingal Head Light.
entries.bio_note: Placement bio supported.

facts.claim: Open 9am-4pm every day of the year, excluding Christmas Day; bookings essential for all tours; entry to the farm marketplace is free.
Guided Farm Tractor Tour and Tropical Fruit Tasting: Adult from A$78, Child (3-16) from A$55, Concession from A$65, infants free.

The tour includes an edible garden path and fruit tasting, a tractor train through the farm (more than 550 fruit varieties), animal feeding at the Fauna Park, a wildlife boat cruise and free time at The Island.
The farm grounds are 215 acres with views of the coastline and Mount Warning (Wollumbin).
The farm operates on NSW daylight time from 4 October 2026 (one hour ahead of Queensland).

facts.claim: Nimbin is a village 30 km from Lismore and an hour from Byron Bay, a centre of alternative lifestyle and culture, sister city of Woodstock, USA.
The 1973 Aquarius Festival revived a dying dairying village; since then it has been a haven for Australia's counterculture.
Wikivoyage See: village main street of alternative-lifestyle shops and cafes, Hemp Museum (gold coin donation), Nimbin Candle Factory, Rainbow Power Company, Djanbung Gardens Permaculture Centre.
Recreational cannabis remains illegal in NSW and police regularly crack down on sales in Nimbin; markets are on the 4th and 5th Sunday of the month.
The original Nimbin Museum was destroyed (fire), per Wikipedia.

facts.claim: Nightcap National Park is part of the Gondwana Rainforests of Australia World Heritage Area, with ancient rainforests, waterways and views of Wollumbin; picnic areas and views from Minyon Falls lookout; camp at Rummery Park campground.

NPWS alert: Nightcap Range Road closed in both directions between Rummery Road and Telephone Road due to a major landslip from the 2022 flood event; affects Minyon Falls lookout, Minyon Falls walking track and Minyon Grass picnic area; access via Minyon Falls Road only; alert applies to 31 Dec 2026.

The park receives the highest annual rainfall in NSW and is often wet and misty; February is the wettest month, September the driest; picnic areas at Minyon Grass, Terania Creek and Minyon Falls lookout.
The 8,080-hectare park was created in 1983 after campaigns and blockades against logging at Terania Creek, Grier's Scrub and Mount Nardi; it is about 35 km north of Lismore.
Highlights include Gidjuum Gulganyi walk, Historic Nightcap walking track, Protesters Falls walking track and Whian Whian mountain-bike trails.

facts.claim: Minyon Falls lookout offers views of the waterfall and rainforest; on a clear day you might see to the coast; easy parking, picnic spots; no public access within 100 m of the top of the falls; falls are most impressive after wet weather.
The walk from the carpark to the lookout is short; asphalt carpark with 2 accessible spaces; unsealed roads, 2WD access; non-flush toilets; no drinking water.
Minyon Falls walking track leads down to the base; Boggy Creek walk leads to Rummery Park campground.
The Minyon Falls plunge more than 100 m over rhyolite cliffs of the old Tweed Volcano.
Wikivoyage lists the lookout as 7AM-6PM, free.
NPWS closed-areas alert (Nightcap Range Road landslip) lists Minyon Falls lookout; access is via Minyon Falls Road only.

unverified: NPWS gives no opening times for the lookout; 7 AM - 6 PM is Wikivoyage (updated May 2024).

facts.claim: Angourie is a coastal village 5 km south of Yamba at the northern tip of Yuraygir National Park.

Angourie Beach was declared a National Surfing Reserve in 2007, the second in Australia; Angourie Point is world renowned for the quality of its waves; Spookies are short hollow right point breaks just to the north.
The Angourie Pools, blue and green freshwater quarry pools less than 20 metres from the ocean, are a popular swimming spot.
Angourie was featured in the 1971 surfing film Morning of the Earth.

facts.claim: Maclean is a town of about 2,800 (2021) on the Clarence River, a very short detour from the M1 Pacific Motorway.

Known as "The Scottish Town" in Australia: street signs in English and Scottish Gaelic, tartan-painted power poles (around 240), a stone cairn in Herb Stanford Park; the Maclean Highland Gathering has been held for over 100 years at Easter.
Wikivoyage See: Maclean District Museum (Tue 9am-noon, Wed Sat 1-4pm), Maclean Lookout over the Clarence River islands, Woodford Island.

facts.claim: Iluka is a small, sleepy beachside village of about 1,800 (2021) in the Clarence Valley; its nature reserve is World Heritage as part of the Gondwana Rainforests of Australia.

Clarence River Ferries runs 4 daily shuttle ferries from Yamba to Iluka Jetty (as of October 2026): 9:30, 11:00, 15:15 and 16:45 (the last does not return that day), plus a 13:45 on Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat; one way A$11.90; none on Christmas Day or Australia Day.
Wikivoyage See and do: Iluka Beach, Queen St Beach, Iluka Museum (Wed Fri Sat 9am-1pm), Iluka Rainforest Walking Track (2.6 km), Bundjalung National Park.
There is no direct road from Yamba without using the motorway (17 km from the Iluka Road exit).

facts.claim: Evans Head is a coastal town and holiday resort on the Evans River, sandwiched between Bundjalung and Broadwater National Parks, with a wide curved beach (Airforce Beach) popular for fishing and surfing; population 2,894 (2021).
Wikivoyage: swim at the river or ocean beach (the ocean beach is occasionally patrolled); lookouts on the south side of town; F-111 Museum (Evans Head Heritage Aviation Museum).
The aerodrome hosts one of the few retired F-111 aircraft in Australia and a museum with authentic aircraft on display.
Bundjalung National Park stretches north from Iluka to Evans Head; park entry fee $8 per vehicle per day.

facts.claim: Byron Bay is a beachside town in far north-eastern NSW, 772 km north of Sydney and 165 km south of Brisbane; Cape Byron, adjacent, is the easternmost point of mainland Australia; population 6,330 (2021 census).

Famed for surfing beaches, scuba diving, whale watching and a laid-back lifestyle; Ballina/Byron Airport is about 30 min away; trains no longer stop at Byron; the nearest rail connection is by coach from Casino.
Ewingsdale Road gets crowded in school holidays and summer; Wikivoyage suggests the Lennox Head exit (Ross Lane) and entering from the south.
Council parking ticket machines charge $2 per hour (Wikivoyage, undated); Main Beach is patrolled all summer.

facts.claim: Ballina is a town and seat of Ballina Shire in the Northern Rivers, 740 km north of Sydney and 185 km south of Brisbane; urban population 46,190 at end 2021.
It is home to the Big Prawn; the Richmond River Light at East Ballina was first lit in 1880 and is still active; settlement began on Shaws Bay in 1842.
Ballina Byron Gateway Airport is about 3.4 km from the CBD (OSM) with flights from Sydney and Melbourne (Wikivoyage Byron Bay).

facts.claim: Tweed Heads is a coastal city at the mouth of the Tweed River, the northernmost town in NSW, 830 km north of Sydney and 103 km south of Brisbane, next to its "twin town" Coolangatta on the Gold Coast.
Wikivoyage: the NSW-Queensland border runs through the built-up area, often not obvious; Gold Coast Airport (OOL) is about 5 km away.
Tweed Heads' most popular tourist destinations include Mount Warning and the nearby Nightcap, Border Ranges, Springbrook and Lamington National Parks.

unverified: Timezone: NSW observes daylight saving (clocks 1 h ahead of Coolangatta, Queensland, from Oct to Apr) - useful as a tip.

facts.claim: Lismore is the main population centre of the City of Lismore LGA and a regional centre of the Northern Rivers.

Wikivoyage: Lismore is more residential than its coastal neighbours, with scenic hinterland drives; the Wilsons River runs through town; a cafe-and-cultures trail starts at the visitor centre and passes the Regional Gallery, historical museum and Back Alley Gallery street art.
Heritage Park miniature train and playground are next to the visitor information centre; Lismore Farmers Market is held Saturday mornings at the showground (weekly market, not a spot).

facts.claim: Yamba is a town at the mouth of the Clarence River; attractions include Yamba Lighthouse (Clarence River Light), Story House museum, the ferry to Iluka, Yuraygir and Bundjalung National Parks and the surf beach at Angourie.

Yamba has one of Australia's most famous surf breaks; about 6,000 people (2016); a stop-off between Sydney and Brisbane; Lovers Point Rock Wall at the north of Pippi Beach is a whale-watching vantage (May to October).
Yamba River Markets run on the 4th Sunday of each month at Ford Park (a monthly market, not a spot).
